key_insight: This paper frames real-time mobile 3D reconstruction as a semantic communication problem, where what matters is not just sending images efficiently, but preserving the scene information needed for accurate reconstruction. The key idea is to make transmission aware of multi-view consistency so pose and geometry estimation remain stable under communication constraints.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of reconstructing 3D scenes in real time from a moving camera while transmitting image streams to a server, where bandwidth limits and communication noise can degrade camera pose estimation and scene geometry recovery.
method: Treats the reconstruction pipeline as a semantic communication task, prioritizing information most useful for downstream 3D scene understanding.
Accounts for on-the-fly camera pose and geometry estimation, where multi-view consistency must be maintained during live capture.
Designs the communication/reconstruction process to reduce sensitivity to communication-induced errors in the transmitted image stream.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more task-aware way to design edge-to-cloud vision systems: optimize what is transmitted based on the reconstruction objective, not just image fidelity. This is especially relevant for robotics, autonomous navigation, and digital twin applications where reliability and latency are critical.

paper_title: Toward Semantic Communication for Real-time Mobile 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Fangzhou Zhao, Yao Sun, Xuesong Liu, Runze Cheng, Shang Kai
